content:
Parent-recorded videos offer a valuable assessment tool for medical diagnoses, as they can be independently rated and compared across various settings. This intervention also shows promise in improving pragmatic language skills by enhancing emotional understanding in children.

Through the inclusion of specific behaviors such as perspective-taking, recognizing emotions, regulating one's own emotions, engaging in interactions, and cooperating to achieve mutual social goals, the assessment evaluates appropriate verbal and non-verbal communication.

To ensure reliable scoring, de-identified videos captured by parents are rated independently by an assessor from various environments, including clinics and homes. This approach supports clinical decision-making for pediatric patients with autism, providing an objective measure of their social communication skills across different settings.
title: A Randomized Controlled Trial of a Play-Based, Peer-Mediated Pragmatic Language Intervention for Children With Autism

content:
Healthcare professionals utilize parent-captured videos in their diagnostic processes. They rate the clinical validity of each video based on factors such as whether additional information is needed for a comprehensive assessment. These ratings inform clinical judgment during remote autism diagnosis assessments, where the videos serve as evidence to support decision-making.

Parent-collected videos can be integrated into the assessment process in several ways. They provide valuable insights during remote diagnostic evaluations, which have been found to be clinically useful by participating diagnosticians. Parents can also assign predefined tags to specific child behaviors in the videos, linking them to relevant DSM subcriteria on a checklist. This streamlined process is facilitated through NODA Connect, which provides access to the child's developmental history entered by the parent.

Parent-captured videos serve as an additional tool for clinicians, offering video evidence of the child's behavior that supports diagnosis and treatment planning through structured review and mapping to diagnostic criteria.
title: A Novel System for Supporting Autism Diagnosis Using Home Videos Iterative Development and Evaluation of System Design
description: Background: Observing behavior in the natural environment is valuable to obtain an accurate and comprehensive assessment of a child’s behavior, but in practice it is limited to in-clinic observation. Research shows significant time lag between when parents first become concerned and when the child is finally diagnosed with autism. This lag can delay early interventions that have been shown to improve developmental outcomes.

content:
Parent-captured videos offer a unique perspective on children's behaviors in natural settings, informing medical decisions for Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) diagnosis. These recordings aid clinicians in making accurate diagnoses by capturing social-communication and play skills in various situations through videoconferencing and mobile/web-based applications.

Parents record 10-minute videos of their child's behaviors at home, providing a more authentic view than traditional in-person evaluations. This naturalistic observation enhances the diagnostic process and may lead to earlier diagnosis.

By contributing a unique, patient-generated perspective, these videos increase the sensitivity and specificity of ASD assessments, supporting clinicians in making informed diagnostic decisions.
